title: Triangle Angle Sum: Mathlib Angle Function Degenerate Cases

problemStatement.plain: Formal investigation in geometry: Triangle Angle Sum: Mathlib Angle Function Degenerate Cases.

currentState.focus: Proof complete: 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Degenerate case analysis fully characterized.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Complete degenerate case characterization: angle sum = π ↔ ¬(p₂=p₁ ∧ p₃=p₁). The standard gallery triangle_angle_sum required p₃≠p₁ unnecessarily — only p₂≠p₁ suffices. Unique exception: all three points equal → sum = 3π/2.
builtItems: triangle_angle_sum_one_cond: angle sum = π whenever p₂ ≠ p₁, for ANY p₃ (TriangleAngleSumOQ03.lean:61)
triangle_angle_sum_p2_eq_p1: p₂=p₁, p₃≠p₁ → sum = π via angle_self_left/right/of_ne (TriangleAngleSumOQ03.lean:71)
triangle_angle_sum_unconditional: sum = if p₂=p₁ ∧ p₃=p₁ then 3π/2 else π, no hypotheses (TriangleAngleSumOQ03.lean:120)
insights: Mathlib angle_add_angle_add_angle_eq_pi only requires p₂ ≠ p₁ — the hypothesis p₃ ≠ p₁ in the gallery proof was redundant
Degenerate Mathlib convention: angle(p, p, q) = π/2 (arccos(0/0) = π/2) — mathematically coherent but geometrically surprising
The only exceptional case is all three points equal; sum = 3π/2 = three right angles each equal to π/2
open Classical is load-bearing: by_cases on Prop requires Classical.em to avoid DecidableEq P typeclass
Oriented angle degenerate cases (oangle) are trivial — angles become 0 — so no interesting analog of this theorem for signed angles
